body: I'm wondering whether it would be better to just include the `$`/`%` in the error message for clarity. (So basically if type type of "$Node" is wrong.)

```suggestion
		const GDScriptParser::CastNode *cast = static_cast<const GDScriptParser::CastNode *>(p_variable->initializer);
```
For all, `auto` is not allowed

That seems like code purity gone to far to me. The version with `auto` is easier to read.

I guess I'll change it for now, but I'd prefer we allow the `auto + static_cast` combination.

Just for reference see [here](https://contributing.godotengine.org/en/latest/engine/guidelines/cpp_usage_guidelines.html#disallowed-features) with explanation, that might seem like a valid exception but where to draw the line?
I don't think we need to discuss this on GH since it's current policy. I'll mark this as resolved and open a discussion on it on RC instead.
